questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

The new product __will be arrive on__ supermarket shelves only next year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'will arrive on'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect. **
 
• Here, **'be' **is used wrongly. We know that when the sentence is in the future continuous tense **'be + V₁ + ing'** is used. But here **'be' **is used without **'ing'** form.
 
• The given sentence is in the **'Future Indefinite'** tense. And using **'ing' with 'arrive'** makes the sentence incorrect.
 
• This tense is used when the action is to take place in **the future. **
 
• The adverbs which indicate future indefinite actions are: **soon, in a few moments, tomorrow, next year/month/week.** 
 
• And we know that the structure of future indefinite tense is: **Subject + shall/will + V₁ + Object. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *The new product **will arrive on** supermarket shelves only next year. * 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The structure of the future progressive tense is as follows: 
 
• The future progressive tense is used when **the action is going on or continuing in the future.**
 
 
• **Subject + shall/will + be + v₁ + ing + object. **
 
 
• *Example: They will be playing chess in the common room. *
 
 
 
 
 
• The future progressive action can be written at **'the point of time'. **
 
 
• *Example: It will probably be snowing when you reach Switzerland. *

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'their'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given question, the **possessive adjective** of **'they', that is, 'their'** should be used. 
 
• It indicates **possession by people or things.** More specifically, **"their" is a possessive adjective. **
 
• It replaces **the noun in a sentence. **
 
• Instead of saying, *"That's the John family's new dog,"* we can say, *"That's their new dog." *
 
• While **"his" **and **"her"** demonstrate **singular possession** (possession by one person), **"their"** is reserved for **two or more people or things. **
 
• In the given sentence **'their'** is used for **all the children of the orphanage. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** "*The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on **their** faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts."*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

It is said that children who learn to use their body, mind, and emotions for their own wellbeing, work ______ the wellbeing of others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'towards'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, **'towards'** should be used. 
 
• Let's look at the meaning of** 'towards'. **It is used differently in different situations:
 
 
• **towards (preposition) (MOVEMENT):**
 
 
• in the direction of, or closer to someone or something
 
• *Example: She kept glancing **towards **the phone.*
 
 
 
• **towards (preposition) (RELATION):**
 
 
• in relation to something or someone
 
• *Example: There has been a change in government policy **towards **energy efficiency.*
 
 
 
• **towards (**preposition**) (POSITION):**
 
 
• near to, just before, or around a time or place
 
• *Example: Our seats were **towards **the back of the theatre.*
 
 
 
• **towards (preposition) (PURPOSE):**
 
 
• for the purpose of buying or achieving something
 
• *Example: The work that students do during the term counts **towards **their final grade.*
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given question, '**towards**' is used to denote a purpose. 
 
• All the other options are grammatically incorrect here because of their different meanings. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *It is said that children who learn to use their body, mind, and emotions for their own wellbeing, work **towards** the wellbeing of others.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Einstein had a deep distaste for enforced learning and was known to skip many of his college lectures.

B. Einstein was also severely critical of the exam-based education system.

C. The great physicist Galileo too said, “You cannot teach anybody anything. You can only help them discover it within themselves.”

D. He often felt that formal education interfered with his natural desire to learn and explore.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ADBC'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of a **Sentence Jumble. **
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually **an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.**
 
• **Part A** will be the first sentence because** it is talking about a past happening. **It talks about **Einstein's distaste for 'forced' learning. **
 
• **Part D **will be the next sentence because **it explains what he felt about formal education.** It seems that Einstein was not happy with the way the education system works. 
 
• **Einstein was critical of **the exam-based education system. Therefore, the next sentence will be **Part B. **
 
• Lastly.** Part C **will be used because what Einstein thinks is also supported by the statement of Galileo. Galileo said that *"You cannot teach anybody anything. You can only help them discover it within themselves".*
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** Einstein had a deep distaste for enforced learning and was known to skip many of his college lectures. He often felt that formal education interfered with his natural desire to learn and explore. Einstein was also severely critical of the exam-based education system. The great physicist Galileo too said, “You cannot teach anybody anything. You can only help them discover it within themselves.”

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

I think Virat Kohli will remain the captain of the Indian team in a year 2020.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'in a year 2020'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The erroneous part **'in a year 2020'** should **'in the year 2020'.**
 
• **'A year'** can be any year without any specification. But **'the year'** means a particular/specified year or the one which is already mentioned and thereby known. 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *In **a year,** there are twelve months. (means any year or all years)*
 
• *I was born in **the year** 2000. (in that particular year)*
 
 
 
 
 
• The given sentence is talking about** a particular year when Virat Kohli will remain the captain. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *I think Viral Kohli will remain the captain of the Indian team **in the year 2020. ***

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** 

 
• **'The'** can be used with **uncountable nouns,** or **the article can be omitted entirely.**
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *I love to sail over the water. (some specific body of water)*
 
• *I love to sail over water. (any water)*
 
 
 
• *​*Do use **'the'** before:
 
 
• **names of rivers, oceans, and seas:** the Nile, the Pacific
 
• **points on the globe: **the Equator, the North Pole
 
• **geographical areas: **the Middle East, the West
 
• **deserts, forests, gulfs, and peninsulas:** the Sahara, the Persian Gulf, the Black Forest, the Iberian Peninsula

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Soon, the idea took its final shape and she started selling barfis under the brand name Harbhajan's and the tagline "You’ll remember your childhood”.

B. That's when Raveena suggested that she should start selling her signature 'Besan ki Barfi'.

C. Today Harbhajan Kaur is truly living by these words as she now sells tasty barfi and makes good money.

D. It all started in 2016 when 94-year-old Harbhajan's daughter asked her if she had any regrets in life, to which she expressed that she never earned a penny for herself.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'DBAC'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **Sentence Jumble.** 
 
• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually **an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.**
 
• **Part D** will be the first sentence because it is the starting of an incident. It is talking about 2016, and the regrets in the life of Harbhajan's daughter. 
 
• **Part B** will be the next sentence because **Part D** talks about *'The regrets in the life of Harbhajan's daughter that she had never earned a penny for herself'* and **Part B** further tells us about **'Raveena's'** suggestion that she could start selling **'Besan ki Barfi'.** 
 
• **Part A** will be the next sentence because** Part B **talks about the idea of selling selling **'Barfi',** and **Part A** further explains **how that idea took shape. **
 
• Lastly, **Part C** will be used because it is a concluding remark. It tells how **'Harbhajan Kaur's' life** has changed. 

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *It all started in 2016 when 94-year-old Harbhajan's daughter asked her if she had any regrets in life, to which she expressed that she never earned a penny for herself. That's when Raveena suggested that she should start selling her signature 'Besan ki Barfi'. Soon, the idea took its final shape and she started selling barfis under the brand name Harbhajan's and the tagline "You’ll remember your childhood”. Today Harbhajan Kaur is truly living by these words as she now sells tasty barfi and makes good money.*

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

We can see much changes in Government schools these days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'much changes'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect. **
 
• The erroneous part **'much changes'** should be **'many changes'. **
 
• We use ***'much'*** with **'singular uncountable nouns'** and **'many'** with ***'plural nouns'. ***
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *I haven’t got **much **change. I’ve only got a ten euro note.*
 
• *Are there **many **campsites near you?*
 
 
 
 
 
• Here, in the given question, the word **'changes'** is quantifiable. And **'changes'** is **a plural noun** also. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *We can see **many changes** in Government schools these days. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• We use the quantifiers **much, many, a lot of, lots of** to talk about **quantities, amounts, and degree. **We can use them with **a noun (as a determiner)** or **without a noun (as a pronoun). **
 
• In informal styles, we prefer to use **'lots of or a lot of'.**
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *I went shopping and spent **much **money. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *I went shopping and spent **a lot of **money. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *

The correct answer is** 'sensed'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here, **the second form of verb** should be used because the given sentence is in **the past tense. **
 
• Because the given sentence is **talking about a past time** when they visited forest. 
 
• Therefore, **'sensed'** should be used here. 

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *After walking a few steps in the forest, our guide **sensed **some sort of movement in the foliage behind us. * 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The usage of **before, after and until:** 

 
 
• We use **before and after** to talk about the order of events in the** past or future.** With **before and after,** either the main clause or the subordinate clause can come first. 

 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *She will pick you up **before **she comes here. *

 
 
• Here, in this sentence **'She will pick you up'** is **the first event.** And **'She comes here'** is **the second event. **
 
 
 
• ***After **she comes here, she will pick you up. *
 
 
• Here, in this sentence **'After she comes here'** is **the first event.** And **'she will pick you up'** is **the second sentence. **
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 'Until' as a time conjunction means up to a time in the past or future. In the case of 'until', the main clause usually comes first.
 
 
• *Example: I’m going to wait **until **the January sales start to buy a new jacket. *
